tasks.spec:
You are authoring a reusable agent SKILL file. You must NOT modify, create, or delete any
file except ./SKILL.md in your own current working directory. Do not run git. Do not commit. Do not
call any MCP tool or App. Do not capture anything to any external system.

Source material is staged INSIDE your working directory at ./source/ . Read it before writing.

WHAT THIS PROTOCOL IS. "Make Sense" is a response protocol for one user. When he says "make sense"
(and not the rhetorical "does that make sense?"), the agent stops answering casually and produces a
structured comprehension artifact: a visible routing declaration, then the artifact in a declared
shape, with every claim carrying a trust marker, an insight section only if it passes three filters,
and a mandatory capture ritual at the end. Version 3.7 adds a fifth pillar called PATH, which is the
forward plan, and PATH is the reason you are writing this file.

WHY PATH EXISTS. Earlier versions produced understanding and then stopped at the edge of "so what do
we actually do." The plan arrived later, in a second pass, in a different vocabulary, and it did not
line up with the two other frameworks the user runs (ATLAS, a typed concept-graph discipline, and
Judge, a verdict discipline for risky actions). PATH folds ATLAS and Judge INTO the Make Sense
response so one output serves all three. The fusion works because the three frameworks already share
bones: a node in ATLAS is a claim in Make Sense is a subject in Judge; ATLAS confidence is the same
axis as a Make Sense trust marker; an ATLAS proof-slot is the same thing as the evidence that would
change a Judge verdict.

THE RULES PATH ADDS, all of which must survive into your file:

1. SPINE. One falsifiable line: what changes, and what counts as won.

2. ONE LADDER, ONE RUNG = ONE GOAL. A rung that delivers no goal is scaffolding, so fold it into the
next rung. A goal spanning two rungs is two goals. This is what keeps a plan to a single ladder
instead of parallel unaligned lists; if it forces a second ladder, the spine is wrong. Render the
ladder as a table, because this user reads tables faster than prose.

3. EVERY RUNG CARRIES SIX LINES. GOAL (what changes for the user, in his language, not the system's)
/ DONE (the binary condition, with a number) / TEST (the exact executable command) / RED (what makes
that command fail) / STATE / WHO.

4. ONE STATE VOCABULARY, replacing three overlapping ones. Proven, building, broken, unknown. This
single set carries ATLAS confidence, ATLAS status, and the Make Sense trust marker at once. An
unmeasured value is unknown and is never assumed to be zero.

5. ONE VERDICT VOCABULARY, from Judge. GO means an agent may act now. HOLD means blocked on something
named. ASK means it needs the human. GATE means an external effect where approval happens at the
moment of action, not in advance. These map to the Judge verdicts allow, block, escalate, and
escalate-at-action.

6. RED IS MANDATORY AND IS THE POINT. A check nobody has ever watched fail is not a check. The
project that produced this protocol version existed because eight quality gates in a media pipeline
could all report success without measuring anything, and five broken releases shipped green as a
result. So every acceptance test must ship with the poisoned input that makes it fail. Where a rung
is a human gate with no machine test, the file must say to write "None - human gate" rather than
inventing a fake one.

7. DECISION BLOCKS LEAD WITH MEANING. Every open decision is written in this exact order: WHAT IT
MEANS in two or three plain sentences, then RECOMMEND, then JUDGE (which judge fired and its
verdict), then WHY (grounded in named data, measurements, or file evidence, never preference), then
IF WRONG (the cost of the recommendation being wrong). The WHAT IT MEANS step exists because the
user pointed out that agents assume he already understands what the question is asking, when the
question's own vocabulary is usually the thing he is missing. Never put a recommendation before its
explainer.

8. PLAN THIS NEXT. When a rung is too big or too uncertain to spec honestly in one pass, say so and
name the single question that would size it. Do not fake a plan for work you cannot yet see.

WRITING REQUIREMENTS.
- Open with YAML frontmatter: --- then name: and description: then ---. The description must state
  when to use the skill and when not to, since that is what an agent reads to decide whether to load
  it.
- Write the whole protocol, not just PATH: the trigger rule, the visible router, all five pillars,
  the output order, the manual shape overrides, and the capture ritual. Someone loading only this
  file must be able to run the protocol correctly with nothing else.
- Include a worked example of a PATH ladder as a table so the shape is unmistakable.
- Style constraints the protocol itself imposes: no em-dashes, no filler words (leverage, seamless,
  holistic), specific numbers over vague claims, tables over prose, challenge over flattery.
- Be complete but not padded. Every line should change how an agent behaves.

THIS IS THE PRIVATE VARIANT, for the user's own machine. ./source/CANONICAL-v3.7.md is the canonical protocol text as installed. Follow it exactly where it is specific.

The private variant MUST point at the canonical text on disk at /home/ankit114/.agents/AGENTS.md and MUST state the load order: search the private brain for the newest captured version first, treat newer captures as superseding the file, and fall back to the file when the brain is unreachable. It may name the user's private systems, because it never leaves his machine.
tasks.verified: a loadable SKILL.md carrying the whole protocol including PATH, with the private constraints honored

THIS IS THE PUBLIC VARIANT, published in a shared skills repository for other people.

./source/EXISTING-PUBLIC-SKILL.md is the CURRENT published version, which predates PATH. ./source/CANONICAL-v3.7.md is the new canonical text. Your job is to produce the next published version: keep what is good in the existing file, add PATH in full, and make the whole thing coherent rather than bolted together.

HARD CONSTRAINT, and the check enforces it: NO private material. No absolute home paths, no private brain product names, no company or client names, no vendor integrations specific to the author. Where the private version says 'search OB_mybcat', the public version says 'search your memory or knowledge system'. Where it names a person, the public version says 'the user'. The framework is the thing being shared; the author's estate is not.
